By Jon Healy

Topic:Cricket

Marnus Labuschagne is dismissed with the final ball of the morning session after Australia chose to bat in the first Test against South Africa.

Recalled opener Nic Maddinson was dismissed for a 33-ball duck in his first Test innings in a decade.

Follow all the action in our live blog below, keep up with all the stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio call on the ABC Listen app.

By Jon Healy

Choose what information you see below by using filters

All

59

Key Events

10

Wickets

4

Comments

5

By Jon Healy

The angle in from around the wicket is threatening the inside edge of Carey, but he keeps the first few out.

No threat of the inside edge on this one as Nortje starts wide and seams wider. Carey throws his hands at it, but misses out.

Another drive with hard hands by Carey, and the ball squirts past point for two more.

By Jon Healy

The off spinner will hope to get some turn away from the outside edges of these two lefties.

Four! Matt Renshaw is paddle sweeping immediately and fine enough to find the boundary.

He tries again and the ball dips under his bat, finding the pad. South Africa goes up for LBW but there's not much going in their favour. Not out and, with only one review left, Temba Bavuma doesn't send it upstairs.

Two more on the lap sweep for Renshaw. Anything full that isn't miles outside off, Renshaw is getting the broom out. Alex Carey will be the same.

By Jon Healy

He angles in to Alex Carey's thigh pad and Carey gloves it onto his thigh pad, but the ball pops up over short leg for a single.

Matt Renshaw drops to the off side and takes off. Credit to Carey for responding and diving in to make his ground. Well played and well run.

That's well blocked out by Carey.

By Jon Healy

And Alex Carey takes a single to the leg side.

Matt Renshaw does the same and that's the 100 up for Australia.

SHOT! A gorgeous on drive for four by Alex Carey. Just a punch perfectly timed. The frustration may be growing for Jansen.

By Jon Healy

He's coming around the wicket to Alex Carey after Wiaan Mulder's success in his last over.

Carey punches a full one hard down the ground and Temba Bavuma dives to get a hand to it. It's a testament to how well struck it was that it still almost made it to the boundary.

Nortje is liking the short stuff to Renshaw. The swing is gone, so the South Africans are starting to use the bouncers. Renshaw is struggling.

By Jon Healy

Renshaw is hit and the ball loops up to Kyle Verreynne. The South Africans are asking the question, but the umpire isn't sure there's glove in it.

He says no. And South Africa reviews.

It looks like this has come off his armguard.

No, I thought there was a rule that if there's no gap between the glove and armguard then it counted as part of the glove, but I guess that's not the rule anymore. Although, maybe there's a tiny gap there.

Also, great bouncer by Jansen. Completely caught Renshaw by surprise.

Jansen settles back into a good line and length outside off, and Renshaw is leaving again. Jansen is right in this fight now.

By Jon Healy

After hours of coming over the wicket and swinging down the line of the stumps to left-handers, Wiaan Mulder comes around the wicket to change the angle to Alex Carey.

Inches! Inches in it as Alex Carey slashes outside off and inside edges between himself and the stumps. There's not a lot of room there, so that must have been very close.

Beaten! A rattled Carey tries to change the line by shuffling down but is once again beaten on the inside edge.

"Why'd he have to dance down? They've got all day. They can be as patient as they want," Shaun Pollock says in commentary on Fox.

By Jon Healy

Well worked off the hip by Renshaw and well run to get through for two runs.

He's leaving well here. Again, the middle order is where Renshaw has found his home in the Queensland line-up, so he may feel a little more comfortable here.

By Jon Healy

A very tight leave by Matt Renshaw to start. Mulder has been swinging it back into the lefties all day, so Renshaw must be very certain to be leaving that close to off stump.

It's another leg bye for the Aussies as Renshaw gets across to try and clip to leg. But it's off the pads again. We will surely be approaching record leg bye levels if this innings carries on like this.

By Jon Healy

Four. Down leg and that's another one just helped on its way for a boundary. Way too easy for Alex Carey.

But Jansen tightens up for the rest of the over.

That's been the experience so far with Jansen. Mostly good, with the occasional wayward delivery.

By Jon Healy

Eight years after getting recalled to the Test team in South Africa in rank circumstances, Matt Renshaw is batting in a Test in South Africa again.

And he gets an absolute gift to get off the mark as Wiaan Mulder sends a ball way down leg and Renshaw just helps it on its way for two.

And then another full one just dabbed to the leg side for a single.

Mulder is still hunting the stumps with the in-swinger to the lefties, but Alex Carey is good enough to drop his bat down in time.

By Jon Healy

And straight away there's a big LBW shout as Marco Jansen spears in at the stumps. But it's going down leg side. So neither the umpire nor the Proteas are all that interested.

Carey survives, but good grief are the Aussies up against it now.

Key Event

By Jon Healy

Australia has lost Marnus Labuschagne and Steve Smith in the space of four balls about 45 minutes apart, as Smith plays back and edges a length ball away to third slip.

After getting smacked on the finger, Smith was playing a long way back there to a ball that really wasn't all that short.

Smith is out for 25 off 53 and, as Alex Carey jogs out to the middle, South Africa has two brand new batters on 0 off 0 to bowl at.

By Jon Healy

Steve Smith is facing the first ball after lunch from Marco Jansen.

Ouch! Second ball after the break rears up at Smith and drills Smith's right index finger, squishing it between the ball and the bat handle.

By Jon Healy

I know this is the men's test blog, but the Aussie women are all class back in brissy!

- Liz

The blokes are battling in Durban, but in Brisbane the women have done it easy in their ODI against Bangladesh.

Annabel Sutherland was player of the match with 4-30 and an unbeaten 25 off 23 as Australia coasted to a seven-wicket win, chasing down Bangladesh's 166 in just over half their allotted overs (25.4).

Phoebe Litchfield top-scored in the run chase with 77 off 57, before Sutherland and Ellyse Perry (26 off 45) finished it off.

Key Event

By Jon Healy

Well, it doesn't get much more painful than that for Australia. After doing all that work to rebuild from 2-24, Steve Smith and Marnus Labuschagne's partnership ends on the stroke of lunch.

It would have been a decent session for Australia had Labuschagne made it through, but in the end the Proteas will be grinning in the sheds as they chow down while Marnus looks for a hole to crawl into.

Key Event

By Jon Healy

Mulder sneaks one past the inside edge and smashes into the front pad. It looks incredibly out, but Labuschagne is taking a review with him after a conversation with Steve Smith.

Oh, he was SO CLOSE to getting outside the line of off stump, but the umpire's call does him in (so Australia won't lose the review) and he has to go for 37.

By Jon Healy

There's a leg gully for Labuschagne. Can Mulder get a ball up into his armpit?

Labuschagne has struggled when he really shuts up shop, so he can't focus too much on just getting to lunch here. Keep playing cricket.

He's getting through. One to come.

By Jon Healy

An edgy single from Labuschagne, and a more assured drive to mid-off to get off strike.

Wide and cut hard to the man on the rope by Labuschagne.

And Smith knocks another one to long-off. They're calming down before lunch.

One more to mid-on by Marnus. Can Smith complete the set with a sixth single?

Nope. A rank wide one is theatrically left alone instead.
